quote: Alright. I had something. You guys just emailed me a quote over.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior touch (a quote already sent) and the rep does not ask which company, what it showed, or why he's calling again.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this as small talk not worth chasing given the call was already moving to verify — but nothing in the transcript supports this as deliberate; it reads as a miss.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what did that quote show you?' immediately — it surfaces competitive context and defuses the 'why are you calling again' irritation.

quote: Black Hills. Those are some of the questions on your fucking questionnaire.
stewart_read: Customer is venting frustration at repetitive intake, and the rep moves straight to the next scripted question with zero acknowledgment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically ignoring the profanity to avoid escalating it — but the immediate hard pivot to the bill question without any softening reads as a missed de-escalation beat, not a deliberate ignore-and-continue strategy.
coaching_implication: A one-line acknowledgment ('I hear you, I'll move quick') would have cost nothing and may have prevented the tone from hardening further.

quote: I don't want it mounted on my roof. I got five acres. I like it mounted on the ground.
stewart_read: Ground-mount request is outside Ion's standard residential-roof install — a real hard-gate scenario, not a soft objection.
coaching_implication: This is a legitimate DQ trigger; the coaching gap is in the delivery, not in the fact of disqualifying.

quote: Okay. We only do roofs and many like, residential roofs for the home. We can't do ground mounts.
stewart_read: Rep states the disqualification with no cushioning, no alternative (e.g., checking on future ground-mount offerings, or a warm close), and no attempt to leave the door open.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have correctly recognized there's genuinely nothing more to offer here — but even a DQ deserves a clean, professional close rather than an abrupt capability statement that reads as dismissive.
coaching_implication: On a hard DQ, close warmly: acknowledge the mismatch, thank them for the info, leave the door open if Ion's offerings change.

stewart_read: Bill captured but the rep only echoes the number back flatly — no emotional flip, no acknowledgment of what $340/month represents.
coaching_implication: Even briefly — 'that adds up over a year, huh' — would have started the alignment-against-utility framing before the DQ ended the call.

quote: Oh, I didn't I'm not interested.
stewart_read: Call ends with no button-up, no next step, and no attempt to check whether a future ground-mount option might exist — the rep just says goodbye.
coaching_implication: Even a DQ close should confirm nothing else is needed and leave a clean professional impression rather than an instant sign-off.
